title: The ‘Exotic Physics’ Behind a Mysterious 1,000-Mile Cloud on Mars
gist: A study in Nature Geoscience led by Jorge Hernández-Bernal of Sorbonne Université is the first to model the Arsia Mons Elongated Cloud (AMEC) on Mars. The cloud grows to more than 1,000 miles each spring and summer morning. The model shows it forming through homogeneous nucleation, a textbook process never before observed in any planet's atmosphere, which requires a 30°C drop in 10 minutes and humidity more than 100,000 times higher than any value measured on Earth.

insights.claim: The Arsia Mons Elongated Cloud on Mars forms every morning during Martian spring and summer and stretches to more than 1,000 miles before dissipating. It had no plausible explanation from its first probe recording in 2018 until a new modeling study.
insights.speaker: Tereza Ondráčková
insights.so_what: This is a long-standing open problem in Mars atmospheric science that has now been addressed.
insights.locator: Every morning during the Martian spring

insights.claim: A Nature Geoscience study proposes that AMEC forms through homogeneous nucleation, where vapor turns directly into ice crystals without dust or salt particles. The process is described in textbooks but has never been observed in any planet's atmosphere.
insights.speaker: Jorge Hernández-Bernal
insights.so_what: This would be the first natural example of a process that had been treated as theoretical.
insights.quote: It’s akin to droplets of condensation appearing in the middle of a room, rather than on a window
insights.locator: The new study, published in Nature Geoscience

insights.claim: Homogeneous nucleation in AMEC requires a temperature drop of 30°C within 10 minutes and very high humidity. Wind hitting the 65,000-foot Arsia Mons volcano creates a strong wave that lifts moist air high into the atmosphere within minutes.
insights.speaker: Tereza Ondráčková
insights.so_what: Topography-driven atmospheric waves are a key mechanism in Mars climate modeling.

insights.claim: The humidity needed for the AMEC cloud is more than 100,000 times higher than any value measured on Earth. Before this modeling, such humidity levels were not known to exist on Mars, and the phenomenon may also occur in the upper atmospheres of Venus or Earth.
insights.speaker: Jorge Hernández-Bernal
insights.so_what: The finding may change assumptions about how much water is in the Martian atmosphere, which matters for future missions.
insights.quote: We don’t have nearly as much information about Mars’ atmosphere as we do about Earth's, so reproducing the AMEC to this degree is a big success
insights.locator: Before this modeling, it was not known
